correctness.rationale: Multiplicativity and the exponent-one sign yield a genuine prefix majorant R and positive tail majorant Z. Finite cylinders and their endpoint conventions are correct by CRT. For fixed k, write Z^k as a product of 1+alpha_p 1_{v_p=1}, alpha_p=(1+1/p)^k-1. In empirical averages, a term for a set of primes is bounded by the product of alpha_p/p using the count of multiples of their product; even with a cylinder indicator the contribution of terms meeting primes above Y is at most exp(S_k)(exp(sum_{p>Y}alpha_p/p)-1). This tends to zero uniformly. Finite-prime CRT and this bound justify the cylinder-weighted infinite moment and Markov bound without any continuity assumption on Z. Strict Z<1/q_i gives the strict reverse comparison. For density existence Trudgian §4 cites Erdős–Wintner for the positive comparison. Independently, the CRT log-ratio model converges in distribution: tail exponents ≥2 occur with probability O(sum_{p>Y}p^-2), and the positive exponent-one log tail has expected value bounded by the same sum. The model is non-atomic: on finite blocks of primes >Y≥3 conditioned on exponents 0 or 1, products of (p+1)/p for different subsets are distinct by the greatest differing prime. Their maximal point mass is at most the product of p/(p+1), tending to zero as the block grows; the omitted higher-valuation event has probability O(sum_{p>Y}p^-2). Independence of the other primes and then Y→∞ give both strict densities. The arithmetic alone does not prove the tail argument or an exact density value.
